terminal.emulator: clean Bash/Fish shells and fresh direct PTYs with deterministic loopback HTTP/SSE

reference.capture: user-local release install, lowercase/capitalized command lookup, and OBS-0094 replay through both aliases

normalization: User home, launcher directory, release binary path, PTY paths, timestamps, process identifiers, ephemeral ports, and raw redraw bytes are omitted or represented by stable markers.

Fresh Bash and Fish shells receive only a synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME and a PATH containing the user-local launcher directory followed by /usr/bin and /bin; shell profiles and configuration files are not read.
Each alias replay uses an isolated HERMES_HOME, a loopback-only HTTP/SSE fixture, and normalized model/request markers; no credential value or external request is recorded.
The lowercase and capitalized aliases are checked separately so a passing debug executable cannot mask an installed-release or command-resolution failure.

steps.precondition: The user-local release binary is installed as hades and Hades in ~/.local/bin.
Fresh Hades launcher process started through the installed hades alias.

input_sequence.value: Select palette-model, submit prompt, fresh-process prompt, Ctrl+C cleanup

steps.precondition: Fresh Hades launcher process started through the installed Hades alias.

input_sequence.value: Select palette-model, submit prompt, fresh-process prompt, Ctrl+C cleanup

unknowns: A shell whose PATH omits ~/.local/bin cannot resolve these user-local aliases; system-wide installation and shell-profile mutation remain outside the contract.
External providers, credentials, OAuth, tools, model catalogs, and network behavior remain outside this release-launcher oracle.
The replay proves the installed artifact carries the bounded vertical slice, not every future Hermes surface or persistent model-selection behavior.
